newsitem.title: USA: US Q2 bank credit card late payments record high.
newsitem.headline: US Q2 bank credit card late payments record high.

text.p: Late payments on credit cards rose in the second quarter to a record high due to fallout from looser lending standards more than a year ago, the American Bankers Association said Tuesday.
Credit card delinquencies were 3.66 percent of the total number of accounts, a 13 basis point jump from 3.53 percent in the first quarter, the banking association said.
The second-quarter credit card delinquency ratio was the highest since ABA began collecting data in 1974.
However, the pace of the increase was slower than in the first quarter when credit card late payments jumped 19 basis points, according to the ABA's Consumer Credit Delinquency Bulletin.
A loan is considered delinquent when it is 30 days or more overdue.
"As expected, credit card late payments are continuing to increase in 1996," James Chessen, ABA's chief economist said.
"The delinquencies being seen today are the result of lending decisions made by banks 18 to 24 months ago," Chessen said in a statement.
Late payments for auto loans made through auto dealers rose to 2.48 percent in the second quarter from 2.13 percent.

That increase help push up the composite ratio of delinquencies for closed-end loans. The composite of eight types of closed-end consumer installment loans rose to 2.32 percent at the end of the second quarter from 2.14 percent, ABA said.
Banks are making an effort to tighten loan standards, but it will take time before that is reflected in the delinquency ratios, ABA said.
"Issuers are cutting back on riskier credit card lending programs, lowering credit limits, lengthening the time between automatic credit limit increases..." Chessen said.
The pace of bank consumer lending was virtually flat with a 0.7 percent increase in the first seven months of this year, ABA said.
"Although loan demand is still strong, consumer borrowing is likely to slow partly due to higher interest rates and banks' tightening of lending standards," the ABA report said.
"While most of the major consumer loan categories are showing increases in late payments, banks are well positioned to handle any losses generated by the delinquencies," Chessen said.
